topic-168-fl-2-overcoming-few-labels-in-.evolution: The collection includes decentralized linear learning and Bayesian neural aggregation, followed by meta-learning-based personalization and domain generalization. Recent representatives use data-free distillation, model mixtures, and interpretable class rules to coordinate heterogeneous clients. These methods approach the same collaboration problem through different exchange formats and assumptions about available data.
openQuestions: Which shared representations transfer without confusing client-specific meanings?
How can personalization benefits be measured fairly for clients with scarce labels?
topic-168-fl-2-overcoming-few-labels-in-.overview: Federated collaboration becomes harder when clients use different architectures, label sets, or local distributions. This topic explores what to exchange: model parameters, generated examples, prototypes, rules, or adapted components. Personalized prediction may require preserving useful local differences rather than forcing every participant into one model.
topic-168-fl-2-overcoming-few-labels-in-.title: Personalization and Knowledge Sharing in Federated Learning
topic-168-fl-2-overcoming-few-labels-in-.whyItMatters: Incompatible representations can make naive averaging misleading, while repeated synthetic distillation can itself introduce drift. Communication efficiency therefore depends on finding a carrier of shared knowledge that clients can interpret consistently.

topic-169-textttshapleig-bayesian-experi.evolution: Representatives include logarithmic opinion pooling in 1997 and later skill models, crowdsourcing quality control, and approval voting. Recent work studies selective aggregation, adaptive group queries, and information-driven Shapley estimation. These are distinct applications of learning from costly partial evidence, rather than one unified voting mechanism.
openQuestions: How can elicitation separate honest uncertainty from unreliable behavior?
Which adaptive queries improve decisions when judgments themselves change with context?
topic-169-textttshapleig-bayesian-experi.overview: This topic combines uncertain judgments from people or models and decides which additional questions are worth asking. Workers may have partial knowledge, inconsistent reliability, or incentives that differ from the requester’s goals. Useful aggregation must therefore model more than a simple majority vote.
topic-169-textttshapleig-bayesian-experi.title: Preference Aggregation and Adaptive Information Elicitation
topic-169-textttshapleig-bayesian-experi.whyItMatters: Expensive judgments should be allocated where they reduce uncertainty about the final decision. Interfaces that permit partial preferences and incentives that reward honest reporting can improve the information collected before any estimator is applied.

topic-170-leveraged-weighted-loss-for-pa.evolution: Early representatives combine labeled and unlabeled observations or group examples into multiple instances. Later work learns from complementary labels, rankings, and proportions. Recent analyses emphasize annotation salience and general-loss guarantees. The common evolution is toward explicitly modeling the annotation process, while the different weak-label settings retain distinct identifiability conditions.
openQuestions: Which annotation biases can be estimated without fully labeled validation data?
How should different weak supervision types be combined without double-counting evidence?
topic-170-leveraged-weighted-loss-for-pa.overview: Supervision can specify less than a full correct label: a class may be ruled out, one positive category may be named, or only group-level proportions may be known. This topic develops learning objectives that use those weaker signals while accounting for the information they omit.
topic-170-leveraged-weighted-loss-for-pa.title: Learning from Incomplete and Indirect Labels
topic-170-leveraged-weighted-loss-for-pa.whyItMatters: Cheaper annotations can broaden access to training data, but missingness is often selective. Treating an unmentioned category as negative or assuming annotations are random can introduce systematic errors that more data alone cannot remove.

topic-171-a-bandit-learning-algorithm-an.evolution: The collection includes finite-time and continuum-action analyses, followed by paid advice, cooperation, and dueling feedback. Recent work develops methods that adapt across stochastic and adversarial regimes and handle decoupled exploration. The theoretical gains depend on the stated feedback model rather than transferring automatically between all bandit variants.
openQuestions: How can algorithms adapt when the feedback regime changes during learning?
When is additional observation worth more than another reward-seeking action?
topic-171-a-bandit-learning-algorithm-an.overview: Bandit algorithms learn while acting under limited feedback, balancing immediate performance with information gathering. The represented work varies what can be observed, whether observations cost money, how delays and corruption enter, and whether exploration can be separated from the action whose reward is earned.
topic-171-a-bandit-learning-algorithm-an.title: Bandit Learning with Flexible Feedback
topic-171-a-bandit-learning-algorithm-an.whyItMatters: These distinctions change the learning problem substantially. A low-regret policy under full feedback may fail when only a selected action is observed, while extra observation channels can make exploration cheaper than ordinary trial and error.

topic-172-a-dataset-for-analyzing-stream.evolution: Early titles concern collaborative filtering; a 2014 model analyzes user-type exploration and nonrepeatable recommendations. Recent work studies sparse pairwise comparisons, open-world representations, and recursive generation of training sequences. The examples broaden feedback and augmentation mechanisms while retaining the core difficulty of inferring preferences from selective observations.
openQuestions: How can synthetic feedback improve coverage without amplifying popularity bias?
Which evaluations distinguish genuine preference learning from reproducing the exposure policy?
topic-172-a-dataset-for-analyzing-stream.overview: Recommendation learns which items suit which users from incomplete interactions, comparisons, or activity sequences. Shared latent structure lets information from one person help another, but observed behavior is sparse and shaped by what the system previously exposed. The topic includes both statistical analysis and practical representation design.
topic-172-a-dataset-for-analyzing-stream.title: Collaborative Recommendation from Sparse Feedback
topic-172-a-dataset-for-analyzing-stream.whyItMatters: Personalization requires learning without repeatedly showing unhelpful items. Synthetic interactions and language models can add information, but may also reinforce existing beliefs unless quality and exposure effects are controlled.

topic-173-a-complete-expressiveness-hier.evolution: The representatives include early learned graph encodings, then formal comparisons of modern graph-network extensions. Recent studies connect expressivity with generalization and investigate truncated positional information. Work on random features for implicit graphs also targets computation without materializing every edge. Together these threads link representational power with the statistical and computational conditions under which it is useful.
openQuestions: When do higher-order structures improve generalization enough to justify their cost?
Which positional encodings remain stable across graph size and sampling changes?
topic-173-a-complete-expressiveness-hier.overview: Graph neural networks must represent structure without depending on arbitrary node order. This topic studies the limits of message passing and the benefits of subgraphs, positional encodings, higher-order constructions, and implicit graph representations. Being able to distinguish more graphs is only one part of successful learning.
topic-173-a-complete-expressiveness-hier.title: Graph Neural Expressivity and Generalization
topic-173-a-complete-expressiveness-hier.whyItMatters: Extra expressivity may increase cost or fit distinctions irrelevant to a task. Generalization analysis asks when richer structure actually improves predictive margins or sample efficiency rather than merely passing an isomorphism test.

topic-174-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.evolution: Earlier representatives approximate adaptive control with local bandit models. Later methods use optimization oracles and unlabeled contexts to make learning practical. Recent work adds large-action-space optimization, adaptive hyperparameters, and stochastic-context incentive mechanisms. These results depend on different context and reward assumptions and should be compared within matching feedback settings.
openQuestions: How can large-action-space optimization preserve the exploration guarantees of the statistical model?
What is the measurable cost of making exploratory recommendations acceptable to users?
topic-174-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.overview: Contextual bandits choose actions using features of the current situation while observing only limited outcomes. The topic studies reductions to supervised learning, large or continuous action spaces, warm starts, paid observations, and incentives for exploration. Efficient optimization is as important as a favorable statistical bound.
topic-174-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.title: Contextual Bandits and Efficient Decision Policies
topic-174-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.whyItMatters: Personalized decisions often have too many possible actions for exhaustive scoring. Moreover, users may not accept exploratory recommendations simply because they help the algorithm learn, making incentive compatibility a separate constraint.

topic-175-a-bio-inspired-redundant-sensi.evolution: The collection includes adaptive motion filtering in 1987 and analog VLSI visual and oculomotor systems through the 1990s. Later work explores redundant sensing and recent time-encoded spike cameras. These examples extend biological inspiration from individual computations to integrated sensing-and-action systems, while remaining distinct from software-only spiking-network training.
openQuestions: Which temporal encodings preserve detail across very different light levels?
How should sensor-level efficiency be compared with end-to-end reconstruction and control quality?
topic-175-a-bio-inspired-redundant-sensi.overview: Neuromorphic vision builds sensing and control systems inspired by biological processing, often using analog circuits or event timing rather than conventional frame pipelines. The representatives connect photoreceptor arrays, motion computation, eye movements, and spike-camera reconstruction. Hardware representation choices directly determine which information is retained.
topic-175-a-bio-inspired-redundant-sensi.title: Neuromorphic Vision and Sensorimotor Hardware
topic-175-a-bio-inspired-redundant-sensi.whyItMatters: Event-based operation can respond quickly to changing scenes, but finite readout bandwidth and dynamic range create constraints. Algorithms and sensors need to be designed together so efficient encoding does not discard the signal needed for reliable interpretation.
